name: Augio: Live undertekster
oneLine: A Danish caption subscription from Glamsbjerg, built for Danish speech: captions on a Windows computer next to Teams or Zoom, on Android and iPhone, and on smart glasses, with one account and a 14-day free trial.

platforms.detail: One account works on a Windows computer, an Android phone and an iPhone, and Augio can show its text on compatible smart glasses (the models are not named). The App Store lists it for iPhone only, not iPad.

deviceRequirements.detail: The iPhone app needs iOS 16.4 or later, and Google Play lists Android 7.0 and up. Which smart glasses work is not stated.

roomCaptions.detail: Put the phone on the table at dinner, in a meeting or in a conversation, and what is said appears as text in real time.

groupConversations.detail: Augio says it works well for conversations between two and three people in an ordinary room, and that five people talking over each other is not something it is good at yet.

languages.detail: Built for Danish speech from the start, with dialects, numbers and everyday language. Its pages mention no other caption language.

offline.detail: Speech recognition runs on servers, so the service needs an internet connection. Augio lists use without internet among the things it is not good at yet.

speakerLabels.detail: Augio's Google Play listing says it can't yet tell who is speaking.

voiceNames.detail: Augio can't yet tell speakers apart, so it doesn't name people by their voice.

translation.detail: Augio's pages describe Danish captions and don't mention translation.

saveTranscripts.text: Yes, encrypted, on your device only
saveTranscripts.detail: Transcripts are stored encrypted on your own device only. The terms say transcripts are only kept if you turn that on, and you can turn it off again.

export.text: Data export when you stop; how not stated
export.detail: The terms say you can export your data when your subscription ends. How, and in which format, is not stated.

fileUpload.detail: Augio's pages describe live captions, not transcribing audio or video files.

summaries.detail: The Google Play listing says you can get a short summary of the conversation afterwards, included in the one subscription. Where the summary is made is not stated.

customWords.detail: Add your own words, such as the names of family, colleagues and places, and specialist terms, so they are spelled right.

display.text: Large text; pause and scroll back
display.detail: Make the text large enough to read at a glance, and pause it to scroll back if you missed something.

soundAlerts.detail: Augio's pages don't describe alerts for sounds like a doorbell or an alarm.

phoneCalls.detail: Augio's pages describe conversations in the room and online meetings on a computer, not phone calls.

videoCalls.text: On Windows, next to Teams or Zoom
videoCalls.detail: On a Windows computer the captions run in a window next to Teams or Zoom, so you don't depend on someone turning on the meeting's own captions.

mediaOnDevice.text: On the computer: online meetings and video
mediaOnDevice.detail: On the computer, Augio captions online meetings, teaching and anything else that happens on a screen. Captioning audio playing on the phone is not described.

humanCaptioners.text: No; not a replacement for a writing interpreter
humanCaptioners.detail: Captions are automatic. Augio says it is a supplement and doesn't replace a hearing aid, a cochlear implant or a writing interpreter (skrivetolk). In Denmark, writing and sign-language interpretation are public services you apply for (borger.dk).

signLanguage.detail: Augio's pages don't describe sign language features.

privacy.detail: Audio is sent encrypted to speech recognition on servers and is not stored. Transcripts stay encrypted on your device. If you agree, words you send to improve its speech recognition are kept under a code that can't be traced back to you. Google Play's data safety section lists email, user ID and purchase history, with no data shared with third parties.

account.text: Yes, email and a one-time code
account.detail: You sign in with your email address and a one-time code, with no password. The same account works on all your own devices.

availability.text: Denmark: Danish App Store, Google Play
availability.detail: Found on the Danish App Store only, not in the US, UK, German, Swedish, Norwegian, Finnish, Dutch or Icelandic stores (November 2026). Prices are in Danish kroner with Danish VAT.

freePlan.detail: A 14-day free trial, once per customer. On augio.dk you register a payment card when you start, and nothing is charged during the trial. After that a subscription is needed.

price.detail: Danish App Store In-App Purchases, November 2026, and the same on augio.dk (card or MobilePay), VAT included. Launch price for subscriptions started before 1 January 2027: DKK 99/month or DKK 999/year, kept as long as the subscription runs.

accessibilityFunding.text: Licences for municipalities and job centres
accessibilityFunding.detail: Augio sells municipalities, job centres and other public bodies a 12-month licence for a named person (DKK 1,200 excl. VAT, by invoice) and offers a named citizen a time-limited trial before a grant. Its pages don't say who qualifies.

strengths.text: Built for Danish speech from the start, with dialects, numbers and everyday language, plus your own words such as family names, places and specialist terms.
One account covers a Windows computer, where captions run next to Teams or Zoom, an Android phone, an iPhone and compatible smart glasses.
Municipalities, job centres and other public bodies can buy a 12-month licence for a named person, with a trial for the citizen before a grant.
Transcripts are stored encrypted on your own device only, and the audio sent for speech recognition is not stored.

limits.text: Its pages describe Danish captions only, with no other language or translation.
Needs an internet connection: speech recognition runs on servers.
It can't yet tell who is speaking, and five people talking over each other is a weak spot by its own account.
No free plan: a 14-day trial, then DKK 149 a month or DKK 1,500 a year (DKK 99 or DKK 999 at the launch price before 1 January 2027).

notes: Conflicts: (1) Transcripts: the App Store listing and Google Play say transcripts are stored encrypted on your own device only, while the terms (21 Sep 2026) say transcripts are only kept if the customer turns that on, that customers can export their data when a subscription ends, and that data is deleted 90 days after it ends; the table follows the store listings and mentions the terms' opt-in. (2) Price: the App Store description and the terms list DKK 149/month and DKK 1,500/year; the pricing page, the App Store In-App Purchases (Augio Pro (lanceringspris) DKK 99 and DKK 999) and Google Play give the launch price DKK 99/month or DKK 999/year for subscriptions started before 1 January 2027. Both are in the table detail. (3) Language metadata: the App Store page and lookup list the app's language as English only (languageCodesISO2A EN), although the listing, website and app are about Danish; the interface language was not checked. (4) Google Play's Danish listing was first published 13 Oct 2026; the App Store release date is 23 Oct 2026. Not found: the app's own privacy policy (augio.dk says it is only inside the app), which smart glasses are compatible, where summaries are made, the Windows system requirements, and any page about translation, other languages, sound alerts, phone calls or sign language. The Android 7.0 minimum comes from the Google Play page's app details data. Testimonials on the homepage were not used. Availability: the lookup API returned the app for Denmark only among dk, se, no, de, gb, fi, nl, is and us; Google Play availability outside Denmark was not checked. borger.dk is used only to describe Denmark's public interpreting. All pages opened 2026-11-02 with curl.
